source.title: Teacher Supervision over Representation Equivalence Classes

page_placements.theme: Representational similarity, functional equivalence and parameter correspondence dissociate

record.tranche_reason: The study uses representation-similarity and alignment measurements in new restoration, cross-width distillation, and grafting experiments. These are conceptual tests of whether representation alignment or mapping corresponds to functional interchangeability, not tests of convergence between independently trained models as scale increases.
record.gate_note: The paper explicitly distinguishes its question from representation-similarity research. Its experiments do not test convergence across scale, modalities, seeds, or universal features. Rows below cover its own measurements of representation similarity across probe domains and its tests of whether feature alignment or mapping preserves model function. Cited prior findings and untested predictions are excluded.
record.test_reason: This is a distillation paper that uses CKA, Procrustes and stitching as tools. Its results concern which training objective restores a teacher's output function. It never measures alignment between independently trained models, across seeds, across scale or across modalities. The restoration students are corrupted copies sharing the teacher's frame. Graft donors are controlled perturbations of the host, and the authors explicitly leave the cross-model test to future work. Result 8 (Qwen2.5-1.5B to 0.5B) trains a projection-based feature loss. It reports perplexity collapse, not how well one model's representations map onto the other's. None of the rows measures what any version names.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that representations are identifiable only up to an orthogonal and isotropic-scaling class, so absolute feature matching is ill-posed. Capability is the output function, and logit matching transfers it while CKA or feature matching alone does not. They also report that feature-only matching collapses even a pristine student in cross-width distillation. Recovery is limited to corpus-covered inputs. Boundary overlap predicts graft success but is necessary, not sufficient. They explicitly do not claim cross-model transfer results.
record.recipe_differences: The paper does not reproduce either original study's convergence method. It uses CKA, Procrustes alignment, feature/logit distillation, and controlled grafting to examine functional transfer and representation alignment.
record.method_sensitivity: Measured CKA varied by probe domain and by whether out-domain text was included in training. Graft outcome also depended on transplant depth; the paper reports failures near the readout despite CKA ≈ 1.00. The experiments do not compare alternative similarity measures systematically.

fits_no_version.finding: Near-perfect CKA (0.999) between a re-initialized copy and its teacher coexisted with destroyed function (perplexity ratio ~3×10^6, top-1 ≈ 0). Logit matching restored function at CKA 0.894.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: High CKA between two networks does not imply functional equivalence; basis-invariant similarity can be high while the output function differs.

fits_no_version.finding: In perturbed-host grafts, boundary CKA predicted success (AUC 0.79), but grafts near the readout failed even at CKA ≈ 1.00.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Seam similarity is necessary but not sufficient for stitching success; layer depth modulates sensitivity.

fits_no_version.finding: CKA recovered by a restoration objective was high in-domain (0.998) but low out-domain (0.533) unless out-domain text was in the training corpus.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation similarity induced by training holds only on the input region the training data covers.

record.problems: The restoration experiments use corrupted copies that share architecture and surviving weights rather than independent models. The graft validation uses controlled perturbations of one model family, not distinct pretrained donors. The cross-width experiments are described as preliminary and modest in scale; one uses a single real model pair and three seeds, and the surrogate uses five seeds. These limits prevent broad conclusions about convergence across independently trained models.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported values on perplexity, top-1, and KL that repeat the same restoration comparisons were not added when they did not measure representation alignment or add a distinct result for V4. Scale comparisons in the restoration tables do not test cross-model convergence. The appendix MLP demonstrations are illustrative of the same coordinate and function distinction, not an additional test of model convergence.

untested.parts: No comparison of independently trained models across size or capability.
No vision–language or paired cross-modal data.
No independently seeded same-architecture models compared for shared features or subspaces.
No mapping or stitching between independently trained models. Grafts use perturbed copies, and the authors defer cross-model grafting to future work.
No interpretable features or circuits compared across models.
No comparison of similarity measures or settings, and no OOD test of convergence between independent models.
No measurement of the degree, plateau or causes of convergence between independent models.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T2 and its V4/V6 labels are not supported. The study's similarity measurements are between a model and its own corrupted or perturbed copy, or are optimization targets of a distillation loss. None concerns convergence or interchangeability between independently trained models. The only genuinely independent pair (Qwen2.5-1.5B and 0.5B) is used for distillation, and the paper reports perplexity, not alignment.

versions.untested_parts: Whether representations of independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, and data become more aligned as size and capability increase.
Cross-modal alignment of paired image and caption representations and its relationship to model performance.
Feature or subspace convergence across independent training seeds of the same architecture.

The experiments test feature alignment and layer grafting in specified settings, not relative representations or mapping without paired data; they do not establish broad interchangeability across independently trained models.
Recurrence of interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits across models.

The study reports probe-domain dependence of CKA and corpus-coverage effects, but does not compare a range of similarity measures or settings such as neighbour counts, nor test general OOD convergence between independent models.
It does not test whether convergence between independent models plateaus or whether shared training data or objectives explain such convergence.

relation.reason: The controlled graft experiment in Section 6 directly measures whether transplanted modules preserve function, bearing on V4. Independent pretraining is explicit in V1–V3 but is not a requirement of V4. The optimized restoration results r1–r4 themselves remain outside the claim versions.

tranche.reason: Section 6 tests module interchangeability through controlled grafting, rather than merely using stitching as a tool. Across 135 grafts, success depends on overlap and transplant depth; near-output grafts fail even at CKA approximately 1.00. This qualifies V4 in the tested setting, without establishing that all possible alignment maps fail.

source_check.notes: Table 3 supports all four rows; its caption explicitly corrects the prose's rounded logit-only agreement to 0.99. Section 7.9 also includes independently pretrained cross-width distillation, contradicting the record's blanket description of the students as restoration copies.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Feature-matching-based capability transfer in the reported restoration and cross-width experiments
reader_labels.reason: Near-perfect CKA or feature matching did not ensure functional interchangeability: Lcka-only matching left capability destroyed (r1–r2), and projected feature matching collapsed the pristine student (r9, r11). Graft overlap was predictive but not sufficient (r12–r13).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Grafting in the controlled same-model-family perturbation setting
reader_labels.reason: Boundary overlap predicted graft success, but the authors report failures even at CKA ≈ 1.00 near the readout; donors were controlled perturbations rather than independently pretrained models (r12–r13).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Restoration measured on in-domain versus out-domain probes, with and without out-domain corpus coverage
reader_labels.reason: CKA was much lower out of domain without coverage, while mixing out-domain text raised it from 0.53 to 0.996; the measured alignment therefore depended on the probe domain and training-corpus coverage (r5–r8).
